title: Xbash_Botnet_Investigation_1e3
description: Investigate and respond to security incidents involving the Xbash botnet, which combines botnet, ransomware, and coinmining capabilities.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these incidents. The network consists of several Ubuntu servers, including a command-and-control (C2) server, two compromised bots, and a victim server. The compromised hosts are running the Xbash botnet, which combines botnet, ransomware, and coinmining capabilities. The botnet uses multiple C2 domains and IPs for communication and can download additional payloads.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the sandbox via the provided cloud environment. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services. The suspicious service is likely named 'system-update-checker.service'. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Understand the concept of systemd services and their role in system management.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system services. Use the command 'systemctl status <service-name>' to check the status of a specific service.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Traffic Service
levels.content: Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.
levels.solution: Examine the network connections and look for any services that are generating excessive traffic. The service responsible is likely named 'bot-flood.service'. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Understand the concept of network connections and how they can be used to identify abnormal traffic.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'netstat -tuln' to check for open connections and look for any services that are generating excessive traffic.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use tools like netstat or ss to check for open connections. Use the command 'ss -tuln' as an alternative to netstat.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution: Identify persistence mechanisms such as systemd timers. The persistence mechanism is likely a systemd timer named 'system-update-checker.timer'. The flag type is a timer name.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Understand the concept of systemd timers and their role in system management.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-timers' to list all active timers and look for any timers associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl status <timer-name>' to check the status of a specific timer.
